Demonstration 2: scATAC-seq Simulation Evaluation

Source: vignettes/demo-scatac.Rmd
demo-scatac.Rmd

Introduction

Single-cell assay for transposase-accessible chromatin sequencing (scATAC-seq) measures chromatin accessibility at single-cell resolution. Unlike scRNA-seq expression counts, scATAC-seq data have unique properties: * High Sparsity: Over 90% to 98% of values in peak-by-cell matrices are zeroes because each locus has at most 2 copies per cell. * Near-Binary Nature: Values primarily represent open (accessible) vs. closed chromatin states. * Peak Co-Accessibility: Genomic loci regulated together exhibit correlated accessibility across cells.

This tutorial shows how to evaluate synthetic scATAC-seq data using scSimEval.

1. Loading the Packaged scATAC-seq Dataset

scSimEval includes an empirical reference and simulated scATAC-seq peak accessibility dataset (example_scatac):

library(scSimEval)

# Load packaged scATAC-seq example data
data(example_scatac)

cat("Reference scATAC-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scatac$ref), "\n")
#> Reference scATAC-seq dimensions: 60 80
cat("Simulated scATAC-seq dimensions:", dim(example_scatac$sim), "\n")
#> Simulated scATAC-seq dimensions: 60 80
cat("Cell types:", levels(example_scatac$cell_types), "\n")
#> Cell types: TypeA TypeB
cat("Batches:", levels(example_scatac$batch_info), "\n")
#> Batches: Batch1 Batch2

The matrices contain integer insertion counts across genomic peaks (60 peaks×80 cells60\text{ peaks} \times 80\text{ cells}).

2. Epigenomic Distribution & Summary Properties

We evaluate whether simulated peak insertion frequencies and cell library sizes match real distributions using evaluate_simulation_accuracy():

atac_res <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(
  ref_data          = example_scatac$ref,
  sim_data          = example_scatac$sim,
  compute_bivariate = FALSE,
  verbose           = FALSE
)
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes

# Inspect peak accessibility and library size statistical distances
head(atac_res$metrics_summary_table, 8)
#>                    Category     Property                      Metric
#> 1 Distributional Properties library_size                 Wasserstein
#> 2 Distributional Properties library_size                          KS
#> 3 Distributional Properties library_size                         MAD
#> 4 Distributional Properties library_size               Bhattacharyya
#> 5 Distributional Properties library_size              Runs_Statistic
#> 6 Distributional Properties library_size                 NN_Mismatch
#> 7 Distributional Properties library_size Between_Dataset_Silh_Global
#> 8 Distributional Properties library_size                         MAE

3. Epigenomic Cluster & Cell-Type Concordance

In scATAC-seq, identifying cell types requires clustering cells based on chromatin accessibility profiles. We test whether the simulator preserves genuine biological separation using evaluate_clustering_metrics():

atac_clust <- evaluate_clustering_metrics(
  data       = example_scatac$sim,
  cell_types = example_scatac$cell_types,
  ref_data   = example_scatac$ref
)

cat("Average Silhouette Width (Simulated):", round(atac_clust$silhouette, 4), "\n")
#> Average Silhouette Width (Simulated): 0.0415
cat("Neighborhood Purity:", round(atac_clust$neighborhood_purity, 4), "\n")
#> Neighborhood Purity: 0.7275
cat("Adjusted Rand Index (ARI):", round(atac_clust$ARI, 4), "\n")
#> Adjusted Rand Index (ARI): 0.5955
cat("Normalized Mutual Information (NMI):", round(atac_clust$NMI, 4), "\n")
#> Normalized Mutual Information (NMI): 0.4934

4. Epigenomic Batch Integration & Confounder Handling

When simulating multi-sample experiments, batch variations can confound biological signals. We evaluate batch mixing metrics using evaluate_batch_metrics():

atac_batch <- evaluate_batch_metrics(
  data       = example_scatac$sim,
  batch_info = example_scatac$batch_info,
  cell_types = example_scatac$cell_types,
  verbose    = FALSE
)

cat("Batch Silhouette:", round(atac_batch$batch_silhouette, 4), "\n")
#> Batch Silhouette: 9e-04
cat("Principal Component Regression (PCR R2):", round(atac_batch$pcr_r2, 4), "\n")
#> Principal Component Regression (PCR R2): 0.0138
cat("Cross-Batch Transfer F1:", round(atac_batch$cross_batch_F1, 4), "\n")
#> Cross-Batch Transfer F1: 0.7347

5. Chromatin Accessibility-Sparsity Curve Dynamics (Category 2)

In real scATAC-seq experiments, peak detection proportion follows a quadratic relationship with mean peak accessibility. We evaluate how well the simulated peak matrix reproduces this accessibility-sparsity curve using evaluate_accessibility_sparsity_curve():

# Evaluate quadratic accessibility-sparsity curve fidelity
sparsity_res <- evaluate_accessibility_sparsity_curve(
  ref_data = example_scatac$ref,
  sim_data = example_scatac$sim
)

cat("Accessibility-Sparsity Curve RMSE:", round(sparsity_res$curve_rmse, 4), "\n")
#> Accessibility-Sparsity Curve RMSE: 0.0123
cat("Quadratic Fit R2 Discrepancy:", round(sparsity_res$r2_discrepancy, 4), "\n")
#> Quadratic Fit R2 Discrepancy: 9e-04
cat("Reference Curve R2:", round(sparsity_res$ref_r_squared, 4), "\n")
#> Reference Curve R2: 0.9693
cat("Simulated Curve R2:", round(sparsity_res$sim_r_squared, 4), "\n")
#> Simulated Curve R2: 0.9684

6. Master Unimodal scATAC-seq Pipeline

Execute the comprehensive evaluation workflow in a single coordinated command:

master_atac <- evaluate_simulation_accuracy(
  ref_data          = example_scatac$ref,
  sim_data          = example_scatac$sim,
  elapsed_time      = 18.2,
  memory_mb         = 512.4,
  compute_bivariate = FALSE,
  verbose           = FALSE
)
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes
#> calcNormFactors has been renamed to normLibSizes

# Inspect tidy summary table
head(master_atac$metrics_summary_table)
#>                    Category     Property         Metric         Value
#> 1 Distributional Properties library_size    Wasserstein  2.3375000000
#> 2 Distributional Properties library_size             KS  0.1750000000
#> 3 Distributional Properties library_size            MAD  2.0000000000
#> 4 Distributional Properties library_size  Bhattacharyya  0.0001055641
#> 5 Distributional Properties library_size Runs_Statistic -6.0273112590
#> 6 Distributional Properties library_size    NN_Mismatch  0.1937500000

7. Conclusion

scSimEval effectively benchmarks scATAC-seq simulations, validating peak insertion distributions, extreme sparsity, cell type clustering, batch mixing, and chromatin peak co-accessibility across the curated evaluation measures suite.
